page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This server features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache configuration of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 480 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. For local storage, it includes a 118 GB NVMe SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. This hardware profile provides a high resource density for memory-bound workloads, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average at 2215.58, whereas the multi-core CPU performance is poor at 2263.98 due to the dual-thread single-core physical layout. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a weak read-only small block cached speed of 168.1 GB/sec, and poor uncached large block read and write speeds of 22.92 GB/sec and 12.15 GB/sec respectively. PassMark CPU and database operations scores are weak, though the PassMark memory score is average at 1927.71. Redis SET operations reach 4.01 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 4.95 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local NVMe SSD, the E2ds_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without demanding heavy multi-core processing power. It is suited for small-scale database hosting, caching layers, light web serving, and basic memory-intensive applications that can leverage its fast local storage and Intel AMX instructions.
